Self-management skills

Organization

Students manage their time, tasks and goals.

For example, they break a task into steps and set dates for each step.

Affective skills

Students manage their attention, motivation and responses to setbacks.

For example, they identify a distraction and plan how to respond.

3 / 8

A shared approach across subjects

Use the same or a very similar tool or strategy in your group, adapted to each subject.

  1. Explore options before choosing your approach.
  2. Record the research sources and why the approach fits your students’ needs.
  3. Plan together on the planning sheet, then refine the planning section in the report.

Complete both planning stages today if possible, or before next week.

5 / 8

Evidence can be flexible

Choose evidence that helps you understand the impact on students.

  • Student feedback
  • Assessment examples or student work
  • Teacher observations
  • Student reflections or self-assessments
  • Before-and-after examples, where available

You do not need every type. Use what is appropriate for your classroom trial.

6 / 8

Initial reflection due: 4 December

Every teacher completes their own reflection in the group report.

A classroom trial is preferred before this reflection. Explain what you tried, what you noticed and your next steps.

If you have not yet tried the approach, reflect on your research and planning. State clearly that it has not yet been implemented.
